rules.rule_context:
From the NJDOL Wage and Hour Compliance unit, as incorporated in Newark CityLink business guidance:

The tip protection rule applies to any person who qualifies as an employer or agent of the employer under N.J.S.A. 34:11-56a4. An employer or agent may not retain any portion of tips distributed through a tip pool, service charge allocation, or direct gratuity, regardless of whether the funds pass through payroll or are handled off-books. The test for agent status is functional, not titular: if the individual performs managerial or supervisory duties that include directing work, scheduling, or disciplinary authority over tipped staff, the individual is an agent for purposes of the prohibition even on days or shifts when they also perform tipped work. The prohibition is all-or-nothing by pay event. An agent who works a tipped shift in a tipped role remains barred from receiving that shift's distribution. The sole lawful configuration for such an individual is payment at a non-tipped base rate with no share of the pool, or, where the employer can segregate pay events by distinct role and the agent performs no supervisory function during that event, participation in the tip pool solely for the non-supervisory role on that event with no crossover in the same pay period.
